clue.text: Case of actress Natalie being digitally enhanced I'm told

indicators.note: I'm told says the pieces are to be heard rather than read, matching the answer by sound

parts.note: Natalie Portman, the American actress, gains a digit, a toe: Portman toe

explanation.surface: Gossip about a court case involving Natalie Portman and some photo retouching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digitally enhanced' looks like photo editing, but a digit here is a toe; PORTMAN plus TOE, said aloud, gives the word for a travelling case.
explanation.definitionFit: A portmanteau is a large travelling bag or trunk that opens into two halves, a kind of suitcase.

clue.text: Previous domestic employee washed up

parts.note: previous means past
a help is a domestic cleaner or servant

explanation.surface: A former maid who is now finished, or who has just done the dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone washed up is finished and beyond rescue, idiomatically beyond saving.

clue.text: Vicar has laser surgery down below in setback

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: REV is short for Reverend, the title of a vicar

indicators.note: surgery reshapes something, so the letters of laser are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman's intimate laser operation goes badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down below' sounds like a coy reference to private parts, but in a down entry it just means the rearranged laser comes after the vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal is a change for the worse in fortune, which is a synonym for a setback.

clue.text: Regularly meet deejay who helped to fleece her father

definitions.text: who helped to fleece her father

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter of the words that follow, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Someone keeps bumping into a DJ who conned her dad out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' sounds like swindling, but it is the Golden Fleece, which Medea helped Jason steal from her father, King Aeetes.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Medea, daughter of King Aeetes of Colchis, helped Jason take the Golden Fleece from her father.

clue.text: More awful retsina drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of retsina are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: Retsina tastes even worse once you've had too much of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, meaning worse or more unpleasant.

clue.text: Some rising go-kart celebrity girl with a daddy complex

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming karting star's girlfriend has issues with her father.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'rising' means read upwards, so the letters inside go-kart celebrity are taken in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra gave her name to the Electra complex, a girl's psychoanalytic attachment to her father.

clue.text: Coppice below Victoria? That's funny

parts.note: below means under
Victoria Wood was a much-loved British comedian, so a funny Victoria is Wood

explanation.surface: Someone spots something odd underneath a woman named Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria Wood was a British comedian and writer; 'That's funny' points to her rather than expressing surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwood is small trees and shrubs growing beneath taller timber, which is what a coppice consists of.

clue.text: See 28
Suave host dominated by sadomasochism

indicators.note: in a down entry, being dominated by something means sitting beneath it, so army comes after SM

parts.note: SM is the usual abbreviation for sadomasochism
a host is a large army

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking party host turns out to be into domination.
explanation.walkthrough: Host here is the old sense of a great army, not someone throwing a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy describes an oily, ingratiating manner, a smooth charm much like being suave.

clue.text: As the UK is now sovereign at last, time they leave the stage

parts.note: after Brexit the UK is no longer in the EU, so it is ex-EU

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of sovereign

explanation.surface: A post-Brexit lament: the UK finally rules itself, so it's time for exits.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the Latin stage direction meaning that several actors go off together.

clue.text: Chester's retired having put away some cash

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Deva was the Roman name for Chester, so Chester's is Deva's

explanation.surface: A man called Chester has retired after building up a nest egg.
explanation.walkthrough: Chester sounds like a person, but it is the English city, known to the Romans as Deva.
explanation.definitionFit: To have saved is to have kept money aside instead of spending it.

clue.text: Flier told to bombard English vice-admiral

indicators.note: told says the pieces are spoken aloud and matched by sound

parts.note: to bombard with artillery is to shell; Sir Francis Drake was vice-admiral of the English fleet against the Armada

explanation.surface: An airman is ordered to attack a senior English naval officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Flier suggests a pilot, but the answer is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelduck or sheldrake is a large duck, a bird that flies.

clue.text: Maker of plant products stocked by kosher Bali store

indicators.note: stocked by says the answer is held within the run of letters of kosher Bali store

explanation.surface: A supplier of plant remedies is carried by a kosher shop in Bali.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbalist prepares remedies from herbs and other plants.

clue.text: Noodle soup; gallons binned by Steptoe & Son?

indicators.note: binned means thrown away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Steptoe and Son was a British sitcom about a father and son who were rag-and-bone men, or ragmen

explanation.surface: Junk dealers throwing out gallons of noodle broth.
explanation.walkthrough: Ragmen collected and sold scrap; dropping their G fits the junk theme of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramen is a Japanese dish of wheat noodles served in broth.

clue.text: Jack Sprat's favourite daughter Eleanor on vacation, a keen swimmer

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Jack Sprat could eat no fat, so he liked lean

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, leaving only the outer letters of Eleanor

explanation.surface: Jack Sprat's favourite child Eleanor is away on holiday, and loves swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' sounds like a holiday but means the inside of Eleanor is vacated, leaving ER.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit Hero, a famously devoted swimmer.

clue.text: Cheese producer working Friday morning around Reading?

indicators.note: working means put to work into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
around says the morning letters go round the R

parts.note: Reading is one of the three Rs, so R

explanation.surface: A cheesemaker hard at work on a Friday morning near the town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading, the English town, stands for R as one of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairy farm keeps cows for milk, the raw material from which cheese is made.

clue.text: A very old western state

explanation.surface: A very old US state out West.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a noun for a US state, but it is the verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to declare or assert openly, which is to state.

clue.text: Prog rock band upset Ms Hird sounding a bit like INXS

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ELP is Emerson, Lake and Palmer, the progressive rock band
Dame Thora Hird was a British comic actress

explanation.surface: A prog rock band annoys actress Thora Hird by sounding like INXS.
explanation.walkthrough: INXS, the Australian band's name, is read aloud as 'in excess', which is what a plethora is.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excessive amount, and INXS spoken aloud is in excess.

clue.text: With which to emphasise writing led by top design?

indicators.note: design means arrangement, so the letters of led by top are laid out anew

explanation.surface: A question about text driven by top-level design.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold type is thick, dark lettering used in print to make words stand out.

clue.text: Drink imbibed by 6 after half time in 1954 classic …

definitions.text: Drink imbibed by 6 after half time in 1954 classic

parts.words: Drink imbibed by 6 after half time in 1954 classic
parts.note: the drink sits inside 6-down's answer, after its first half

explanation.walkthrough: 6-down is UNDERWOOD; split at half time into UNDER and WOOD, the drink goes in the middle to make Dylan Thomas's Under Milk Wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk is a white drink from cows, the beverage inserted in the title of the Welsh play.

clue.text: Artist Paul reportedly drinks this well known brand

parts.note: Paul Klee was a Swiss-German painter

indicators.note: reportedly says the pieces are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to neck is British slang for to drink quickly, so drinks gives necks

explanation.surface: Paul Klee is said to drink a famous brand of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' turns necks, British slang for downs quickly, into its sound-alike ending for the tissue brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Kleenex is a famous trademark for paper tissues, a household brand name.

clue.text: … screened by Amalfi deli opposite opera

indicators.note: screened by says the answer is concealed behind the run of letters of Amalfi deli opposite

explanation.surface: Continuing 18: the milk is kept out of sight at a deli in Amalfi across from the opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidelio is Beethoven's only opera, a work for the stage set to music.

clue.text: Desperate French caper

parts.note: a caper is a playful antic

explanation.surface: A desperate escapade carried out in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic means wild with worry or haste, a state close to desperation.

clue.text: Brown dog mess?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the dog of William Brown in Richmal Crompton's Just William books
second meaning: a disordered heap, a mess

explanation.walkthrough: Brown is not a colour here but the surname of William Brown, the schoolboy hero of the British Just William stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumble is a confused, untidy mixture, and also the name of William Brown's mongrel.

clue.text: Question one: Crikey: evens or odd?

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: evens says take the second, fourth and sixth letters of Crikey

explanation.surface: A quiz question: crikey, is it evens or odds?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evens or odd' looks like a betting choice; evens is the instruction and odd is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Quirky means unconventional or peculiar, a synonym of odd.

clue.text: Punitive lending policy universal in Amtrak?

indicators.note: in says the universal letter sits inside the railway letters

parts.note: Amtrak is a US railway, so US plus RY, the abbreviation for railway
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Is a punishing loan policy standard on America's passenger trains?
explanation.definitionFit: Usury is lending money at exorbitant interest, a punishing credit practice.

clue.text: Came round, had a meal wrapped in papers, wasted

indicators.note: round says the letters of came are turned about into a new order
wrapped in says ate goes inside the papers

parts.note: ID, short for identity documents, means papers
had a meal means ate

explanation.surface: Someone regained consciousness and ate a fish supper wrapped in newspaper, while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' suggests drunk in the surface, but here it means thin and starved.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin, wasted away through lack of food or illness.

clue.text: Gruffudd drinking whiskey from Des Moines?

indicators.note: drinking says one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: Ioan Gruffudd is a Welsh actor
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Actor Ioan Gruffudd drinking whiskey made in Iowa's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Des Moines is the capital of Iowa.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iowan is a native of Iowa, the US state whose capital city is Des Moines.

clue.text: Mum with a hint of gel in hair which is attractive

indicators.note: in says mum plus the hint of gel sit inside the slang word for hair

parts.note: Barnet is cockney rhyming slang for hair, from Barnet Fair
Ma is an informal word for mum

indicators.note: a hint of picks just the first letter of gel

explanation.surface: Mum, with a dab of gel in her hair, looks lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNET, cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), holds MA and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar magnet is a straight magnet, something that attracts iron in a literal sense.

clue.text: Wife slimy when befuddled with drink

parts.note: oozy means slimy or muddy

explanation.surface: A wife becomes sloppy when she has had too much to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Woozy means dazed or unsteady, as one is when tipsy.

clue.text: Palace watch City taking the lead

indicators.note: taking the lead says the city's letters go first, ahead of the watch piece

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
to watch is to see

explanation.surface: Crystal Palace supporters watch Manchester City go ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Palace and City look like football clubs; Palace is the Paris residence of the French president.
explanation.definitionFit: The Élysée is the palace in Paris that serves as the official residence of the French president.

clue.text: Examine VW breaking down touring California — it's the fans playing up

indicators.note: touring says the scrambled letters go round CA
a car breaking down falls apart, so the letters of examine VW are scrambled

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: Inspecting a broken-down Volkswagen on a Californian road trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Fans suggests a cooling fan in the car, but these are sports spectators rising in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican wave is a crowd of spectators standing and raising their arms in sequence round a stadium.
